title: The trypan blue cellular debris assay: a novel low-cost method for the rapid quantification of cell death
author: Lebeau, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Prepare complete medium
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the complete cell culture medium at 15,000 × g for 5 min to remove particulates, then warm the medium to the desired temperature before use.

steps.title: Seed cells in 6‑well plates
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the pre‑warmed complete medium to each well of a 6‑well tissue‑culture dish and seed approximately 8 × 10⁵ cells per well (≈80 % confluency), ensuring equal cell numbers across wells.

steps.title: Treat cells
steps.instruction: Apply the desired drug(s) or experimental intervention to the seeded cells and incubate for the required treatment period.

steps.title: Harvest cell‑debris‑containing medium
steps.instruction: After treatment, gently collect all medium from each well with a pipette without disturbing adherent cells, transfer the medium into pre‑labelled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, and set aside for debris isolation.

steps.title: Pellet cell debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collected medium at 10,000 × g for 2 min at room temperature. If weakly adherent live cells are present, first spin at 500 × g for 1 min, discard the supernatant, then repeat the 10,000 × g spin. Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Stain debris with trypan blue
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 0.4 % w/v trypan blue solution (or 400 µg trypan blue dissolved in 100 mL distilled water) to each tube, vortex to resuspend the pellet, and let the mixture stand at room temperature for 5 min.

steps.title: Wash stained pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 × g for 2 min at room temperature, discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, then add 500 µL of 99 % isopropanol, gently invert the tube, and remove the isopropanol wash with a pipette while avoiding pellet disturbance.

steps.title: Extract trypan‑blue stain
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of PBS to each tube, vortex to resuspend, place the tubes in a dry‑block heater at 80 °C for 10 min, then centrifuge (same conditions as above) to pellet debris and retain the blue‑coloured PBS supernatant.

steps.title: Measure optical density
steps.instruction: Transfer 45 µL of the blue PBS extract into technical duplicate wells of a 96‑well plate, then read absorbance at 590 nm using a spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Prepare assay controls (optional)
steps.instruction: For a blank control, add 100 µL trypan blue to a tube containing no debris and process as above; for a 100 % cell‑death control, freeze a parallel culture dish at –80 °C for 20 min, collect all debris by scraping, and stain using the same protocol.

description: Here, we describe a non-invasive method, referred to as the trypan blue cellular debris (TBCD) assay, to examine media content of cell debris occurring as a result of cell death. Following the harvest of debris, live adherent cells can continue to be grown or be utilized for additional assays. Although the following protocol was optimized using 6-well tissue culture dishes, the protocol can also be optimized for use with other culture dish formats.
